newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain gives details on Repsol share offer.
newsitem.headline: Spain gives details on Repsol share offer.

text.p: Spain's state holding company SEPI said on Saturday it would offer 12.75 million shares in energy firm Repsol SA to retail buyers at a four percent discount in the initial phase of its upcoming share offer.

SEPI, which is selling its remaining 10.001 percent stake, said it was initially offering 22.95 million shares or 7.65 percent with 2.55 million so-called "green shoe" shares in reserve for oversubscription and 4.5 million for employees.
The holding company, which approved details of the share offer late on Friday, said it would offer 2.04 million shares to Spanish institutional buyers and 8.16 million to international investors.

The subscription period begins on Monday, April 7 and runs through April 21 at which time the maximum share price will be set. The final price will be set on April 28 and shares will start to trade on the bourse the following day.
The global coordinators for the share offer are Spanish banks BBV and Banco Santander and U.S. investment house Goldman Sachs.

This is the fifth share offer for the energy group, which was formed in 1987 our of a reorganisation of state stakes in the petroleum and gas sector. The last placement was in February 1996, when 11 percent of the group was sold for 4,147 pesetas retail and 4,335 pesetas intitutional.
Repsol shares closed up 20 pesetas at 5,840 on the Madrid bourse on Friday.
